newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota's Pomeroy says 1.7 mln acres under water.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota's Pomeroy says 1.7 mln acres under water.

text.p: Approximately 1.7 million acres of North Dakota cropland were under water due to flooding and much of that acreage will not go into agricultural production this growing season, Congressman Earl Pomeroy said Sunday.
"Normally they'd be working their farms now and putting their crop in in mid to late May," he said. "Obviously there's going to be land that simply will not be capable of planting."
Pomeroy, Democrat of North Dakota, made his comments at a joint news conference of local, state and federal officials.

"When you consider that 40 percent of North Dakota's economy is directly derived from agriculture, this will have an ongoing, devastating effect to our economy that will still be continuing long after people are back in their homes," Pomeroy said.

Pomeroy described how the thaw of record winter snowfall had had caused the severe flooding along the Red River Valley. But he said crop production was not the only area of agriculture suffering effects of the brutal winter weather.
"Through the winter and including this last blizzard, we lost better than 10 percent of our livestock," he said.
